senses: One who, or that which, slaps.
ety: From slap + -er. For senses 2 and 3, the OED tentatively quotes the Bloomsbury Dictionary of Contemporary Slang: "This working class term from East London and Essex is probably a corruption of shlepper or schlepper, a word of Yiddish origin, one of whose meanings is a slovenly or immoral woman."

senses: A type of pungent Turkish tobacco.
ety: From Latakia (“the Syrian port from where the tobacco is shipped, and near where it is produced”), from Arabic اللَاذِقِيَّة (al-lāḏiqiyya).

senses: A moderately hard blue cheese, from Spain, made from goat or sheep milk
ety: Borrowed from Spanish cabrales. The milk of the cheese comes from cows farmed in the Asturian municipality of Cabrales.

senses: Able to be irrigated.
A fish, a California chimera (Hydrolagus colliei, syn. Chimaera colliei).
A hairstyle characterized by a long lock of tail-like hair dangling from the back of the head; the dangling lock itself.
A type of file (cutting tool) with a round cross section and usually also a taper toward the distal end.
An excrescence growing from the pastern to the middle of the shank of a horse.
The flowering plant Stachytarpheta cayennensis.
ety: From rat + tail: all of the nonliteral senses come from something else's fancied resemblance to the tail of a rat.

senses: A member of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, an Indian nationalist paramilitary volunteer organization.
ety: From Hindi स्वयंसेवक (svayansevak), from Sanskrit स्वयम् (svayam, “self”) and सेवक (sevaka, “servant”).

senses: That makes a twanging sound.
examples: There’s an occasional schmaltziness, aggravated by the overuse of a twangy score, but more than enough moments of genuine heartbreak, joy and suspense to make up for it.

senses: inland, towards the mountains.
ety: Borrowed from Hawaiian mauka (“landward, shoreward (from the sea), towards the inland”).

senses: One who, or that which, warps or twists out of shape.
Mendacious boasting that lacks seriousness; falsehood or humbug, especially when it is told mockingly or without the expectation that anyone believes it.
ety: Borrowed from French blague. Doublet of belly.
examples: The difference is this: one may be obliged to maintain a falsehood from feelings of pride or self-respect, but a blague can be given up without a scruple.
The blague differs from the laughter of, say, Hugo's L'Homme qui rit, just as it is distinct from irony, which is never coarse or untrue, and indeed presupposes a whole shared system of values.
But whereas blague, as Pound seems to envisage it, begins with pomp and ends in derision, this poem emerges from circumstances of derision

senses: A rural poem; a poetical composition on husbandry, containing rules for cultivating land, etc.
ety: From Latin georgicum, georgicus, from Ancient Greek γεωργός (geōrgós, “farmer, earth worker”), from γῆ (gê, “earth”) (combining form γεω- (geō-)) + ἔργον (érgon, “work”).

senses: A leader or conductor of a musical group such as an orchestra.
Person in charge of music at a noble court during the baroque and classical period.
examples: The daily routine of the Hofkapelle was normally entrusted to the Kapellmeister. This was the most important musical position at court.

senses: A person who is contacted by someone.
A person who has been contacted by alien beings from outer space.
examples: He believes the contactees (those who claim to have actual contact with beings from outer space) are actually creating a new theology.
The “contactees” or “saucerians” surfaced in 1952 in southern California. They presented themselves as selected by superior beings from other planets for a special assignment—save the world.

senses: A person of Hawaiian descent.
A South Pacific Islander, especially a labourer in Australia or Canada.
ety: 1840. From Hawaiian kanaka (“person”), ultimately from Proto-Polynesian *taŋata.
examples: It was considered one of the nation’s strictest bans because of the reference to Kanakas – native Hawaiians – and because Nevada was the only other state to add Chinese.
The Kanaka at the wheel gave him a glance, but did not speak.

senses: The water of life; the drink of the Hindu gods.
ety: From Sanskrit अमृत (amṛta, “immortal, immortality”). Compare also Ancient Greek ἀμβροσία (ambrosía, “ambrosia”).

senses: The work done by a farrier.
A farrier's workshop.
consisting of two cones placed together apex to apex
A person who explores their own psyche, commonly with the aid of psychedelic drugs.
examples: It has also become an influential subculture in the Bay Area, where devotees commonly refer to themselves as effective altruists in the same way they might describe themselves as leftists or psychonauts.

senses: The practice of traditional Hawaiian adoption of one child into another family.
Of a person: able to be extradited.
Of an action or an offense: for which one can be extradited.
Decorated with spangles; sparkly.
A monetary tribute formerly paid to the bishop or archdeacon, at the time of his Easter visitation, by every parish priest.
A constitution made in a provincial or diocesan synod.
ety: From Middle English synodal, synodall, from Latin synodālis. By surface analysis, synod + -al.

senses: Most fish in the Pomacentridae family.
A period of quiet, rest and relaxation, especially after a party, etc.
Synonym of downtempo.
One who plays the harpsichord.
examples: Some harpsichordists might have dismissed these works as not “authentic” Handel, Mr. Cooper said, though he surmised that the arrangements could have been prepared by Handel’s students.

senses: Having a grain or grains.
Stained with an imitation wood grain.
Having a specified type of grain.
ety: From grain + -ed. Piecewise doublet of corned.

senses: legal, juridical, pertaining to the law and jurisprudence
Synonym of doofus.
Synonym of couesnophone.
ety: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from goof + Latin -us, possibly taking its ending from ignoramus.

senses: The doctrine that free will and determinism are compatible ideas.
One who or that which flays.
Synonym of robustness.
To release (gaseous substances) into the air, especially of a polymer material as it is aged or heated.
Describing a light vegetable sauce, especially one served with pasta.
A stripe, usually one of a set of parallel stripes.
One of the fillets between the flutes of columns, etc.
A stretch mark.
One who or that which formats.
examples: In this exercise, you will override conneg and let ASP.NET Web API use the media formatter that you specify to serialize the resource.

senses: A substance that suppresses.
The degree of being retardant
examples: The methods for evaluating flame and fire retardancy of these materials have been already established.
Fire safety legislation dictates, in particular, designing products of high-flame retardancy along with minimal environmental impact.

senses: A person of mixed Brazilian Indian and European or African descent.
ety: Borrowed from Brazilian Portuguese caboclo, borrowed from Old Tupi kuriboka.
examples: Dawn found him still awake, in one of the two taverns of Cumbe, drinking brandy with sour cherries and having a ballad contest with the caboclo Matias de Tavares.

senses: A Vedic yajña (ritual or sacrifice) mentioned in the Atharvaveda and performed in orthodox Hindu communities.
ety: From Sanskrit अग्नि (agni, “Agni”) + होत्र (hotra, “sacrifice, burnt offering”).

senses: Unaffected by time; timeless; permanent or unchanging.
examples: The machinery, when activated, would create atemporal bubbles wherein nothing was affected by the flow of time.
